summary: The root visual node of a Router page component: declares the page's title, URL pattern and meta tags.
description: Page is the mandatory root of every page component shown by a Router (Page Router) — a Router only mounts components whose graph contains exactly one Page node. It is not in the node picker because the editor creates it automatically when a page is added to a Router; there is no replacement node, you configure the existing one. Its `title` sets the document title and the Router's `currentPageTitle`; its `urlPath` is the page's URL pattern and may contain `{param}` placeholders that Page Inputs (PageInputs) nodes read; the remaining inputs are SEO meta tags (description, robots, og:*, twitter:*, sitemap hints) plus padding and CSS styling for the page surface.
whenToUse: Do not add Page from the node picker or use it outside a Router page component — it is created automatically as the root when a page is added to a Router. Edit that existing node to set the page's title, `urlPath` and meta tags.

ports.onPageReady: Signal input; the SSR handshake. Pulse it once the page has the data it needs and the SSR server releases the rendered HTML.
ports.done: Signal; the page has announced that it is ready to render.
ports.completed: Signal; fires after Done. No Failure or Unchanged — announcing the event cannot fail and every pulse announces.
ports.title: String value; the page title, shown as the document title when the page is active. Defaults to the component name.
ports.urlPath: String value; the URL pattern that routes to this page, e.g. "product/{productId}" — placeholders become path parameters readable via PageInputs. Defaults to the title, lowercased and hyphenated.

runtimeBehavior: Runtime-determined inputs (runtime-discovered): an editor connection re-sends `title` and `urlPath` per instance so the property panel can offer defaults derived from the component name. Both are ordinary declared inputs and are settable as parameters with no editor attached: the exporter reads them off the node into the router index, so a headlessly authored page carries its own title and URL. Nothing else on this node is runtime-determined.
